title: Humyn Labs Raises $47M to Teach Robots How Humans Work
dek: The Bengaluru startup films real chores and jobs to train robot AI models.

facts.label: Venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton

caption:
Robots can't learn to fold laundry from the internet. So one startup is filming people doing it. 🤖

Humyn Labs, a Bengaluru-based robot training data company founded in early 2026, just raised $47 million in Series A funding: $26M in equity led by Accel plus $21M in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. Its head-mounted camera rigs record real workers and household chores across 20+ countries, then label hand positions, object contact and depth so robot models can learn from them.

Why it matters: physical AI needs data that doesn't exist online, and most of Humyn's customers are US AI labs and humanoid robot makers. The company claims $50M in annualized revenue within six months, though those figures aren't independently verified.

We're tracking the race to train humanoid robots daily at AI Parabellum. Would you let a camera record your chores for robot training?
